solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Phrasebook with 'wreath containing cross'? That's got to mislead

indicators.note: containing tells us the wreath word holds the cross letter inside it

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland or wreath of flowers
X is the shape of a cross
to con someone is to mislead or swindle them

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about a phrase book entry describing a wreath with a cross in it, suspected of being a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The words 'That's got to' are only link words; the question mark flags the playful framing of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicon is a word list or dictionary, loosely a book of phrases and vocabulary.

clue.text: Revival of drug test oddly exposing testosterone type

indicators.note: revival read as re-vival suggests bringing something back the other way, so the letters are read backwards
oddly asks for the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the words drug test

explanation.surface: A drugs test after a comeback exposes a muscle-bound athlete's testosterone use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes D, U, T, S from 'drug test' and 'Revival of' turns DUTS round; 'exposing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is slang for a virile, macho man, one full of male hormones.

clue.text: A smallholder ultimately practised kind of farming

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of smallholder

parts.note: practised, as in skilled, means able

explanation.surface: A small farmer has finally taken up a particular style of agriculture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives R, the last letter of 'smallholder'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable land is used for growing crops, so arable farming is the crop-growing kind.

clue.text: Disaster immediately on the news

indicators.note: news is spoken by a broadcaster, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: right off is an idiom meaning straight away or immediately

explanation.surface: A catastrophe is reported straight away on the news bulletin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the news' signals that RIGHT OFF, meaning immediately, is said out loud and heard as a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete failure or a vehicle damaged beyond repair is called a total loss, a disaster.

clue.text: Belligerence stands out in uppity oaf

indicators.note: in tells us the phrase for standing out is placed inside the other piece
uppity in a down clue means the word goes upwards, read from the bottom

parts.note: a slob is a lazy, oafish person
something that stands out shines or excels

explanation.surface: Aggression is conspicuous in an arrogant lout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uppity' turns the lout round; 'in' sets the shining phrase inside. Bolshy is British slang for stroppy and uncooperative.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshiness is combative awkwardness, a stroppy and aggressive attitude.

clue.text: The Flying Horse's soft sausage rolls lacking original character

parts.note: p for piano is the musical marking meaning soft

indicators.note: rolls suggests tumbling the letters about into a new order
the original character of the alphabet is the letter A, and lacking says it is taken away

explanation.surface: Seemingly a winged steed's soft sausage rolls, missing their first ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking original character' removes A from SAUSAGE to leave SUSAGE, which 'rolls' rearranges as EGASUS after P. The 's after Horse stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the winged horse is named Pegasus, also a constellation.

clue.text: Blair finally dragged into his old school in chains

indicators.note: dragged into tells us the letter is put inside the school name

parts.note: Fettes College in Edinburgh is the private school Tony Blair attended

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of Blair

explanation.surface: Former prime minister Tony Blair being hauled back to his old school in shackles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives R from 'Blair', and 'dragged into' puts it inside FETTES; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetters are shackles for the feet, so chains in the sense of restraints.

clue.text: Judicial examiner getting gold returned — he may be happy to go on record

definitions.text: he may be happy to go on record

indicators.note: getting the precious metal returned means that part of the word is turned round
getting the precious metal returned means that part of the word is turned round

parts.note: a coroner holds inquests, examining deaths in a judicial role

explanation.surface: An official investigator receives gold back; he may be glad to give evidence on the record.
explanation.walkthrough: CORONER contains OR, heraldic gold; 'gold returned' reverses it to RO. The definition plays on 'record' as a gramophone disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A crooner is a singer of sentimental songs, who would gladly be heard on a record.

clue.text: Indicator of onset of rain stopping unexpected heatwave over north-east

indicators.note: stopping says the letter plugs a gap within the jumbled word
unexpected suggests the letters arrive in a surprising order
onset of points to the first letter of rain

explanation.surface: A sign of rain coming that interrupts a surprise hot spell blowing in from the north-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpected' rearranges the hot spell as WEATHEVA, and 'stopping' plugs the R (from 'onset of rain') into it; 'over' just places the compass point below in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A weathervane shows wind direction, so it is an instrument that points or indicates.

clue.text: Queen conceivably protected by most uncivilised creature

indicators.note: protected by means the royal insect sits safely inside the other word

parts.note: wildest is the superlative of wild, meaning untamed or uncivilised
a queen bee is one kind of bee, so conceivably signals an example

explanation.surface: A monarch shielded by the most savage beast imaginable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen conceivably' is a definition by example: a queen is one kind of the insect, hence the question of conception.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnu, an African antelope, is one specific animal.

clue.text: Dispute among characters in 'Flaubert's Parrot'

indicators.note: among characters in tells us the letters are found within the title's letters

explanation.surface: An argument among the people in Julian Barnes's novel Flaubert's Parrot.
explanation.walkthrough: Characters here are letters, not people in the novel: the answer runs across 'Flaubert's Parrot'.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to argue or exchange blows, as in a dispute.

clue.text: Without her Olympic chief's not in short articulate

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the name goes around the pronoun

parts.note: Seb Coe headed the London 2012 Olympics organising committee
n't is the shortened form of not

explanation.surface: Lacking her, the Olympics boss is not, briefly, well-spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' in its old sense means outside. Lord (Seb) Coe is a British former Olympic runner who chaired the London 2012 organisers.
explanation.definitionFit: Coherent speech is clear and well-expressed, the adjectival sense of articulate.

clue.text: Sweeping hit for six nothing short of vexatious, eh?

indicators.note: hit for six means knocked flying, so the letters are scattered and rearranged
short of nothing tells us the letter for zero is removed from the pool

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A thorough rout seen as a ball hit for six, utterly vexing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing short of' takes O from VEXATIOUS EH, and 'hit for six' rearranges what remains. In cricket a ball hit for six is struck over the boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeping survey covers everything, so it is thorough and complete in scope.

clue.text: Loathsome one of the Smiths less than tuneful

indicators.note: less than tells us the comedian's name is subtracted from the longer word

parts.note: melodious means tuneful or pleasant to hear
Mel Smith was a British comedian, so Mel is one person named Smith

explanation.surface: A hateful member of the band The Smiths sings out of tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less than' removes MEL from MELODIOUS. The surface suggests the Manchester band The Smiths, but this is Mel Smith, the British comic actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or repugnant, a direct synonym of loathsome.

clue.text: Peanuts that may get scattered around Dorking?

definitions.text: Peanuts that may get scattered around Dorking?

parts.words: Peanuts that may get scattered around Dorking?
parts.note: Dorking is a Surrey town but also a breed of hen, so grain scattered for poultry; peanuts also means a trifling sum

explanation.surface: Nuts strewn about a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorking is a town in Surrey, England, and also a breed of domestic fowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain for poultry also means a very small amount of money, which peanuts means too.

clue.text: Parky's visit creating unexpected buzz

parts.note: parky is British slang for chilly, cold
to call on someone is to visit them

explanation.surface: Michael Parkinson, the chat-show host called Parky, drops in and causes a surprising stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parky' looks like the TV host Michael Parkinson but is British slang for cold weather. A buzz is a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsolicited sales telephone call, a ring you were not expecting.

clue.text: Dense Romeo overwhelmed with uncontrolled desire

indicators.note: overwhelmed with means the letter is swamped, sitting inside the other piece
uncontrolled suggests letters running wild into a new order

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dim lover consumed by unbridled passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncontrolled' rearranges DESIRE as SERIED, and 'overwhelmed with' puts R inside, after SER.
explanation.definitionFit: Serried ranks are closely packed together, so crowded or dense.

clue.text: Inexperienced? Not with us getting hardened

indicators.note: not with tells us the letter standing for with is dropped

parts.note: callow means young and inexperienced

explanation.surface: Losing your innocence alongside us makes you tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes W from CALLOW to give CALLO, then US; 'getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone callous is unfeeling, emotionally toughened or hardened.

clue.text: Succeeded with identical-sounding follow-up

indicators.note: sounding says the letters built here are only heard, giving a similar spoken word

parts.note: S abbreviates succeeded and identical means equal

explanation.surface: Success came with a follow-up that sounded the same.
explanation.walkthrough: S (succeeded) with EQUAL, said aloud, gives a word heard like the answer; 'sounding' is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequel is a later book or film that continues the story, a follow-up.

clue.text: On reflection most of Etna is uneven and alien

indicators.note: on reflection, as in a mirror, means the letters are read backwards
most of says the letters are taken from inside the phrase, not using all of it

explanation.surface: Thinking it over, much of the volcano Etna is rough and strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' says to read 'Etna is uneven' backwards, and 'most of' takes the run of letters inside it; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venusian is an imagined inhabitant of Venus, so a being from another planet.

clue.text: Ignore closing seconds of unwelcome heckle

indicators.note: ignore closing means the final letters are left off

parts.note: needless means unnecessary or uncalled for, hence unwelcome
S is the abbreviation for second, so seconds gives two of them

explanation.surface: Disregard the last moments of a rude interruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignore closing' removes the two final S letters (seconds) from NEEDLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle is to provoke or goad someone, much as a heckler does.

clue.text: Guitar part giving trouble

definitions.meaning: a ridge across the fingerboard of a guitar
to worry or be troubled, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: Fret names both the raised bar on a guitar neck and the act of worrying.

clue.text: She's picked on Conservative leader in articles in Germany, Spain and France

indicators.note: leader points to the first letter of Conservative

parts.words: articles in Germany, Spain and France
parts.note: der, el and la are definite articles in German, Spanish and French

explanation.surface: A woman victimised by the Tory leader within articles from three European countries.
explanation.walkthrough: C (the Conservative leader) and IN, then DER, EL, LA: 'the' in German, Spanish and French.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale the heroine is bullied by her stepmother and stepsisters.

clue.text: Alpha male with chronic fatigue syndrome turning up for work

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the whole sequence is read from the bottom

parts.note: Alpha is A in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ME, myalgic encephalomyelitis, is another name for chronic fatigue syndrome

explanation.surface: A dominant man with an exhaustion illness shows up for his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses AMME, read from the bottom of the down light. The definition is a literary work, Jane Austen's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a novel by Jane Austen, a literary work.

clue.text: Dicky reviles fawning

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for weak or faulty, so the letters are unsound and rearranged

explanation.surface: Dicky criticises someone obsequious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' reads as a name but is the British adjective for shaky or unreliable, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Servile behaviour is slavishly obsequious, the same as fawning.

clue.text: Uproar about student love affair

parts.note: C, from Latin circa, means about
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a British learner driver's car
an amour is a love affair

explanation.surface: Public outcry over a scholar's romance.
explanation.walkthrough: C (circa, about), L (learner, student) and AMOUR side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamour is loud outcry or noise, much like an uproar.
